top_drivers: U.S. long-end Treasury yields remain elevated, with the 10-year around 5.3% and the 30-year near multi-decade highs, preserving dollar rate support.
Brent crude is back above $100, restoring some yen-negative terms-of-trade pressure.
USDJPY recovered into the 158.3 area after falling below 158, showing resilience despite Japan-side wage and BOJ-normalization support.
The broad U.S. dollar was firmer ahead of the FOMC minutes.
counterevidence: The 158.50-158.51 area rejected price once already today, so upside resistance is active.
Japan 10-year yields are also higher, providing some yen support through the rate channel.
Japanese intervention sensitivity rises as USDJPY approaches 159.
The 03:00 JST FOMC minutes could be less hawkish than current long-yield pricing and trigger a dollar/yield reversal.
scheduled_catalysts_known_pre_cutoff: 2026-10-08 03:00 JST FOMC minutes for the September 15-16 meeting.
2026-10-08 04:00 JST Federal Reserve G.19 Consumer Credit release.

scenario_map.base: Range-to-slight-up: USDJPY ends 08:00 modestly above its 22:00 level, with high U.S. yields and oil outweighing Japan-side support.
scenario_map.upside: Hawkish FOMC minutes or continued long-yield pressure pushes USDJPY sustainably above 158.5 toward 159.
scenario_map.downside: FOMC minutes are less hawkish than priced, Treasury yields fall, and USDJPY mean-reverts below 158.0-158.1.
